title: From Complex Histories to Simple Predictors: Predictive Dimension in Dynamic Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.28090v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing continuous-time graph learning methods rely heavily on complex neural architectures to encode ever-expanding interaction histories. However, the future conditional distribution induced by complex histories can often be characterized by a low-dimensional predictive state manifold, implying that only a few predictive degrees of freedom are essential for future interactions. We therefore argue that continuous-time graph learning should identify low-dimensional states sufficient for future prediction rather than reconstruct the full history. To make this perspective measurable, we define and independently estimate the intrinsic predictive dimension, which quantifies the effective predictive degrees of freedom required by a given task. translated_title: 从复杂历史到简单预测器：动态图学习中的预测维度
translated_abstract: 现有的连续时间图学习方法严重依赖复杂的神经架构来编码不断增长的交互历史。然而，由复杂历史所诱导的未来条件分布通常可以用一个低维的预测状态流形来刻画，这意味着对于未来的交互而言，只有少数预测自由度是关键的。因此，我们主张连续时间图学习应当识别对预测未来而言充分必需的低维状态，而不是重建完整的历史。为了使这一观点可度量，我们定义并独立估计了内在预测维度，该维度量化了给定任务所需的有效预测自由度。具体而言，我们从以历史为条件的未来分布中去除与历史无关的边缘分布，分解由此得到的预测残差算子，并估计其最小有效秩……
tldr: 该论文提出连续时间动态图学习无需重建完整交互历史，而应识别足以预测未来的低维状态，并定义了可独立估计的“内在预测维度”来量化任务所需的有效预测自由度。
en_tdlr: The paper argues that continuous-time dynamic graph learning should identify low-dimensional states sufficient for future prediction rather than reconstruct full histories, and introduces the intrinsic predictive dimension to independently quantify the effective predictive degrees of freedom required by a given task.
